brief_data.deck: Together AI, the San Francisco cloud built for open-source AI, closed an $800M Series C at an $8.3B valuation on 1 July 2026, led by Aramco Ventures with Nvidia, Vista and General Catalyst: two and a half times its February 2025 price, with annual bookings past $1.15B.

risks.label: CROWDED ARCHETYPE
risks.detail: CoreWeave, Core Scientific and Groq already hold grid positions; a fourth AI-cloud logo can read as a follower.
risks.counter: Make Haas the first team whose compute story is open-source inference, and price it as a product deal.

risks.label: INVESTOR TIES, NOT PARTNER TIES
risks.detail: Aramco's F1 money sits at Aston Martin, where CoreWeave holds the lane; the warm path leads to the ecosystem, not to Haas.
risks.counter: Use Aramco for the F1 introduction; sell Haas on product use and the US rounds.

gridfit.label: OPEN
gridfit.detail: no rival in this category lane

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Vipul Ved Prakash before the United States GP to test appetite for a first sports partnership, agree an Austin or Las Vegas announcement window, and size an Official AI Cloud Partner entry against the Haas 2027 roster.

value.text: Together Instant GPU Clusters are self-service and spin up in minutes; the Frontier AI Factory offers dedicated Blackwell clusters at scale. For Haas that means on-demand capacity for machine-learning surrogates, strategy and driver-in-the-loop simulation, and telemetry and video analytics between sessions, without capital tied up inside the cost cap.
value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)

value.text: Open models fine-tuned on the team's own documentation and data, served from private endpoints, give engineers and strategists assistants that never send team data to a third-party model. That is the concrete product a team without a hyperscaler partner cannot buy cheaply elsewhere.
value.label: Private inference for the engineering office

value.text: Together sells to developers, CTOs and hyperscalers. Its guest list at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas is enterprise buyers, investors and bankers: the audience Haas's B2B partners (Mphasis, CommScope, Infobip) want in the suite.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Official AI Cloud Partner designation, sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, hospitality at the three US rounds, and co-produced engineering content from Kannapolis for Together's developer channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 1 July 2026 Together AI announced an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. This is a company release, not a press report, so the figures are confirmed.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed in February 2025. Annual bookings passed $1.15B in the quarter before the Series C, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. A company re-priced that fast, selling to developers and enterprises, has a story to tell and a budget to tell it with.
why_now.label: Price up two and a half times in sixteen months

why_now.text: Management says the infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years. An infrastructure brand is built while the capacity is built: the enterprise buyers, bankers and hyperscaler partners it must win are exactly the audience an F1 paddock assembles.
why_now.label: A build-out that needs a name

why_now.text: Brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. The United States GP in Austin (October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US stages on which a San Francisco company would announce. Since this brief's date, IBM signed a $240M multi-year agreement (11 August 2026) to host a Together AI inference cluster on IBM Cloud from the first quarter of 2027, which strengthens the capacity story rather than changing the recommendation.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: The Haas technology roster is Toyota Gazoo Racing (title), Mphasis (IT services), CommScope and Ruckus (networking) and Infobip (cloud communications), joined in July 2026 by Exein for device-level security. There is no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner: Official AI Cloud Partner is a clean category, and Haas partnerships are priced below the front of the grid.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Haas is run from Kannapolis, North Carolina, and is the only US-owned team on the grid until Cadillac's arrival this season. A San Francisco company gets a home team for Miami, Austin and Las Vegas and a story that plays to the US enterprise market where its customers sit.
why_team.label: The American team

why_team.text: A team without a hyperscaler partner buys its compute at list price. Elastic GPU clusters for surrogate models, simulation and analytics, and private inference for engineering assistants, are consumed in the factory rather than displayed on the car, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.
why_team.label: A team that will use the product

why_team.text: Aramco, the round's lead investor, is F1's Global Partner and the title partner at Aston Martin through 2028, so the sport already knows the name. That path leads into F1, not to a specific team: at Aston Martin the lane belongs to CoreWeave, which is why the recommendation is Haas.
why_team.label: The ecosystem path

ruled_out.reason: CoreWeave, Official AI Cloud Computing Partner since May 2025, is a direct rival; Aramco's title deal does not open that lane.
Core Scientific and TWG AI occupy the compute and AI lanes on the 2026 roster.
Google Cloud, Dell Technologies and Groq cover cloud, hardware and inference silicon.
Oracle is title partner and the cloud and AI incumbent.
Microsoft holds the cloud lane at both; Mercedes also carries Hewlett Packard Enterprise, AMD, G42 and Meta AI.
HP (title) and IBM cover compute hardware and cloud services; IBM is also now Together's own cloud host, which would make the roster conversation awkward rather than warm.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise on the roster in the last 12 months; lane crowded.
Open compute lane but not chosen: Williams' AI story is Claude's, a closed model, and VAST holds the data platform; Together's brand is open-source inference.
Open but not chosen: Dynatrace and Confluent hold the data lanes, and there is no US identity to match a San Francisco company.

brief_data.bottom_line: An $800M round at $8.3B, bookings above $1.15B and a 50-fold build-out put Together AI at peak brand-investment authority with an F1-literate lead investor. The compute lane at TGR Haas is open and the US rounds sit inside the planning window.

score_cells.note: Round closed 1 Jul; Austin and Las Vegas inside the year.
score_cells.label: TIMING

score_cells.note: Developer-facing B2B brand; Aramco and Nvidia on the cap table.
score_cells.label: BRAND FIT

score_cells.note: 50-fold build-out and Q4 rosters; no hard deadline.
score_cells.label: URGENCY

score_cells.note: MODE A: self-service GPU clusters and private inference.
score_cells.label: OPS FIT

brief_data.the_case_p1: Together AI announced on 1 July 2026 an $800M Series C at an $8.3B post-money valuation, led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia, March Capital, Pegatron and S Ventures. Annual bookings topped $1.15B in the last quarter, with thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon. The $305M Series B at $3.3B, led by General Catalyst, closed only in February 2025. The company says its infrastructure footprint will grow roughly 50-fold over five years: for an infrastructure business, the brand-building moment arrives with the build-out.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The grid has already priced the neocloud archetype: CoreWeave became Aston Martin Aramco's Official AI Cloud Computing Partner in May 2025, Core Scientific and TWG AI opened on Cadillac's first roster, and Groq holds inference silicon on McLaren's. Aramco, the lead investor here, is both F1's Global Partner and the Aston Martin title, so the ecosystem knows the name; the seat, though, has to be one CoreWeave does not already hold.

brief_data.industry_meta: AI Infrastructure · Open-Source AI Cloud / Inference
brief_data.value_content: MODE A - operational. A team without a hyperscaler partner buys compute at list price. Together's self-service GPU clusters spin up in minutes for machine-learning surrogates, strategy and driver-in-loop simulation, and telemetry analytics between sessions; private open-model inference gives engineers assistants that keep team data in-house. In return: a named compute partnership, sidepod presence, and Miami, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Together's enterprise buyers.
brief_data.why_team_para: Haas is the American team, run from Kannapolis, North Carolina, racing in 2026 as TGR Haas F1 Team under Toyota Gazoo Racing's title partnership. Its technology roster is IT services, networking and communications: Mphasis, CommScope, Ruckus, Infobip. There is no cloud, GPU or AI-compute partner, so Official AI Cloud Partner is a clean category at the grid's most accessible price. A San Francisco developer brand gets a US home team, three US rounds and engineers who will use the product.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official AI Cloud Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the 50-fold build-out and a probable listing window. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-payable in compute credits. Scope: sidepod or engine-cover placement, naming of the team's compute environment, US-round hospitality, engineering content.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 1 July; brand budgets are set in the quarter after a raise, and a 50-fold capacity plan needs a name enterprises recognise. Teams fix 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter; the United States GP (Austin, October) and Las Vegas GP (November) are the stages for a US announcement.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Prakash co-founded Together AI in 2022 after selling Topsy to Apple and leading search and AI for Siri; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Kai Mak, Chief Revenue Officer, Charles Zedlewski, Chief Product Officer, Meicheng Shi, SVP Finance. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Vipul, your lead investor is F1's Global Partner, and CoreWeave took its Aston Martin seat the year it listed. The American team has no compute partner. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
